edges.description: Reduced GRHL3 transcriptional output disrupts formation and differentiation of the embryonic oral periderm.
A functional periderm prevents the apposed oral epithelia from adhering to one another; a dysfunctional periderm permits pathological adhesions.

nodes.description: GRHL3 encodes the grainyhead-like 3 transcription factor, which governs differentiation of stratified epithelia. Dominant disease-associated variants reduce or abolish its transcriptional activity; missense variants identified in Van der Woude syndrome acted as dominant negatives in a zebrafish periderm assay, while truncating variants cause loss of function.

evidence.snippet: GRHL3 is a transcription factor that plays an important role in primary neurulation and in the differentiation of stratified epithelia of ectodermal or endodermal origin

nodes.description: The oral periderm is a transient, single-cell-layered epithelium that forms early in embryogenesis and expresses polarised adhesion complexes. GRHL3 (together with IRF6, under p63 control) is required for its formation; loss of GRHL3 produces an abnormal oral periderm.

nodes.description: Without an intact periderm barrier, intimately apposed and adhesion-competent oral epithelia fuse pathologically, obstructing the orderly elevation and midline fusion of the palatal shelves.
